_comment: Italian synonym groups for the live quiz's same-language mode (src/lib/liveQuiz/questions.js). Every word in a group can stand in for every other one in an everyday sentence (iniziare / cominciare domani); a word may sit in more than one group, and the quiz never offers a synonym of the prompt as a wrong option. Where the words differ in register, the group is still interchangeable in meaning, and `nota` says how they differ (English, not shown yet). level = the level a learner meets the group at; pos steers the wrong options (a verb is asked among verbs). Nouns carry the article (il/lo/la/l'). Standard Italian; variety it-IT on every group. idioms-mistakes run (2026-11-14), not yet reviewed.

groups.nota: Both are neutral. cominciare is a little more common in speech, iniziare in writing and at work.
terminare is a little more formal: the meeting terminates, I finish the pasta.
macchina is the everyday word. auto is a bit more neutral or written (on signs, in the news, la patente auto).
soldi is the everyday word (plural only). denaro is formal and written.
Same meaning. ora is a little more formal; ora also means hour.
papà is used everywhere. babbo is typical of Tuscany and parts of central Italy.
domandare is a little more formal. Both take a person: chiedere a qualcuno.
bimbo is warmer and more informal, often used for small children.
abitazione is the word in forms and notices (residenza, abitazione principale).
impiego is more formal and used for office jobs. Everyday speech says lavoro.
acquistare is more formal (shops, ads, contracts). In speech: comprare.
Both mean fast. rapido often describes a short time or a quick action: una risposta rapida.
complicato describes something with many parts. difficile is more general.
semplice also means plain, without frills.
immediatamente is stronger and more formal.
frequentemente is more formal and typical of writing.
medico is the neutral word. dottore is how you address a doctor: Buongiorno, dottore.
abito is a bit more elegant: un abito da sera, un abito da sposa.
comprendere is more formal and often about ideas or reasons.
attendere is formal: attendere in linea, attendere il proprio turno. In speech: aspettare.
errare is literary or used in set phrases (errare è umano). In speech: sbagliare.
timore is more formal and milder.
ditta is common for small companies, azienda for any size. società is the legal word.
via is used in addresses (via Roma). strada is the road itself.
perciò is a little more formal than quindi. dunque often starts a conclusion in speech.
immenso also fits abstract things: un dolore immenso.
rinviare is more formal: the hearing is postponed. In speech: rimandare.
modificare is formal and used for documents, plans and settings.
consentire is more formal, typical of rules and signs.
suggerire is gentler and often about ideas, consigliare about advice.
conseguire is formal, used for degrees and goals (conseguire la laurea).
domanda is also the application you submit at an office (la domanda di cittadinanza). richiesta is a general request.
